start.text: A collier's clamp rake has been driven into the waymark's cairn beside the post, iron head up, tines hanging, the way you'd plant a stake to say somebody's been here.
The pole is notched. On one side, an A, cut deep. On the other, a T, cut deeper. And above them, newer, a single notch cut clean across both sides at once.
Abe and Tolly Dray's rake. They never once agreed whose it was. It seems they did, here, or agreed to leave it.
Two colliers' marks on one rake. Whoever they were, they left it standing, pointing north.
